Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office receives ordinary paperwork, assigns reference numbers, and files documents in chronological order. Each entry lists a field, a verification check, and a sign-off. Unverified items remain flagged pending review, and duplicates are noted when serial numbers repeat across files.

2) What occurred: On a dated record, the actor entered a valid ticket identifier into a duplication request document; the uniqueness check field stayed unverified. The actor then created several matching document copies in a batch output file; the source-field integrity sign-off stayed unverified. The actor transmitted the copies to a buyer channel before the gate; the transfer-receipt field stayed unverified. The actor adjusted the queue-position field on the gate-pass document; the authorization sign-off stayed unverified. The actor disabled the refund-request flag in the transaction record; the reversal-approval field stayed unverified. The actor suppressed chargeback alerts in the payment channel log; the dispute-review sign-off stayed unverified. The actor removed the identification requirement from the entry document; the identity-verification field stayed unverified.

3) Materials/access observed: A named account, a dated record, a batch output file, a buyer channel, a gate-pass document, a transaction record, a payment channel log, and an entry document.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Repeated serial numbers across the batch output file, a missing uniqueness check on the duplication request, a queue-position edit without authorization sign-off, a disabled refund flag without reversal approval, suppressed dispute alerts, and a blank identity-verification field on the entry document.
